intent: Schematic diagram scene: a 5,614 km wire fence draws itself across the frame while a km counter ticks, then reveals the continental split — arid north above, fertile south below.

beats.action: On a quiet banded ground (arid tones above, green tint below), the fence wire begins drawing left-to-right as a km counter counts from 0 upward — the audience immediately understands a distance is being measured.

The wire continues its run across the full safe width, fence posts snapping up one by one along its path, the counter climbing toward 5,614 km; the soft zone tint under the line deepens as 'FERTILE SOUTH' appears beneath.
At full extent, a small benchmark tick appears beside the counter: 'longer than the Great Wall'.
Final hold: the whole fence line gives one slow shimmering pulse (dashed wire animation) continuing into the cut, counter locked at 5,614 km.

handoff.opening: Deliberately replaces any footage-based opening: the scene opens as a pure measured schematic — hard reset from any live-action neighbor, the drawn line itself is the hook.
persistentElements: The horizontal fence wire motif (can reappear as a divider or route line in the next scene)
handoff.endState: Full fence line drawn across safe zone at y≈500, counter locked at 5,614 km left-aligned, 'FERTILE SOUTH' pill below the line, Great Wall benchmark tick visible, gentle wire pulse in motion.
handoff.motionVector: Left-to-right drawing energy just resolved; the residual shimmer travels rightward along the wire, inviting the next scene to follow the fence's path into the landscape.
handoff.nextOpportunity: Next scene could match-cut from the schematic wire to real footage of the actual fence, inheriting the horizontal wire as a transition line.
